chapter: Chicago, Virginia Ravens and the northern territory bands
title: The Doo Dads from Ditty Wah Ditty and duets with Lester Young
summary: Back in Minneapolis he led a small band with a comic-strip name. Lester Young joined him in Minneapolis and the two played school dances as an alto and tenor duo.

bands.name: Doo Dads from Ditty Wah Ditty

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Still in '27. Because all of this happened, you know -- but we stayed over through into '28. And through the winter. And that next spring we left Bismark and came back to -- I came to Minneapolis with this group. And then I got me, finally organized me a little band. In fact, Roy was the trumpet player, and myself -- I have the letterheads at home now, called -- we got together and organized a little group called the Doo Dads from Ditty Wah Ditty. Now, where the name come -- in those days they used to have

a comic strip called the Doo Dads. I know you don't remember it, but it was these little people like the Seven Dwarfs. And that word Ditty Wah Ditty was a slang word, we used to say, you know, if you're going to some place out of the world called Ditty Wah Ditty. So we named our little band the Doo Dads from Ditty Wah Ditty.

And we got a job playing for a dance marathon up in MINOCWA Minopie- (DUNNETTE) Wisconsin. Of course, before then Lester Young had left his father's band and came to Minneapolis playing tenor. And that's when he and I used to get together, just the two of us, and play school dances just with the sax es alto and tenor and no rhythm or nothing. Just played the two of us.

Yeah, in the spring. So we got this little band, it was Roy White and Jimmy Farris on trombone and I was playing alto. And Leon Lewis was the drummer. And we had Merle Williams again on piano. I have pictures of him. And a fellow named Charlie Odin on bass, playing tuba. MINOCWA
